title: Nirsevimab versus placebo for medically attended RSV lower respiratory tract infection in infants
topic_state: POOLED -- risk ratio, k=2 (placebo-controlled subset); 1 seeded trial excluded and stated
provenance: REGISTRY THROUGHOUT. Counts and denominators read from ClinicalTrials.gov posted results.
verification_basis: All THREE seeded registrations read on 2026-08-18 including arm types and posted results.

pooled_hartung_knapp.why_it_is_shown: Handbook 6.5 section 10.10.4.5 recommends Hartung-Knapp where k is small. Shown ALONGSIDE the unadjusted interval, not instead of it. A FLOOR OF 1 is applied to the variance-inflation factor so the adjustment can never NARROW the interval below the unadjusted one.

heterogeneity.DIRECTION_TEST: NOT APPLICABLE -- I-squared is 0.0%, below the threshold at which the direction test is informative. The trials are consistent with a common effect and no heterogeneity caution is warranted. Applying one here would manufacture doubt the data do not support, which is the mirror failure of ignoring heterogeneity that matters.
heterogeneity.how_to_read_this_at_low_k: At k=2 or k=3 these statistics are weak evidence about consistency in EITHER direction. A low value means the estimates are CONSISTENT WITH a common effect, not that one is demonstrated.
heterogeneity.tau2_estimator: REML -- copied from this block's declared `estimator`, which is the authoritative record of how the pool was computed. NOT inferred: an object that declared no estimator would be left undeclared here, because the absence is itself the finding.
heterogeneity.i2_definition: UNDECIDABLE from this object. I-squared is 0 and Q is below the degrees of freedom, where the Higgins form is negative-and-clamped and the REML/metafor form is exactly zero -- BOTH DEFINITIONS GIVE 0 and nothing here distinguishes them. Recorded as undecidable rather than guessed.

per_trial.label: Phase 2b
per_trial.how: RR = (e1/n1)/(e2/n2); SE(log RR) = sqrt(1/e1 - 1/n1 + 1/e2 - 1/n2), Handbook 6.5 section 6.4.1. Counts read from the registry; only the arithmetic is ours and the formula is shown.

per_trial.label: MELODY
per_trial.how: RR = (e1/n1)/(e2/n2); SE(log RR) = sqrt(1/e1 - 1/n1 + 1/e2 - 1/n2), Handbook 6.5 section 6.4.1. Counts read from the registry; only the arithmetic is ours and the formula is shown.

primary.outcome: medically attended RSV lower respiratory tract infection
primary.the_third_trial_EXCLUDED_and_why: NCT05437510 (HARMONIE) IS SEEDED ON THIS PAGE AND IS NOT IN THIS POOL. Its comparator arm is typed NO_INTERVENTION and titled 'No preventive intervention' -- an OPEN-LABEL UNTREATED control, not a placebo. The two pooled trials are PLACEBO_COMPARATOR and double-blind. An untreated open-label control cannot be pooled with a blinded placebo control on a MEDICALLY ATTENDED endpoint, because whether a carer seeks medical attention is exactly the kind of outcome unblinding moves. Its counts are recorded so the exclusion is checkable: nirsevimab 11/4038 against no intervention 64/4019.

published_synthesis_comparison.what_is_owed: No published synthesis or regulatory review of the nirsevimab programme has been read.

primary.what_this_does_not_establish: NOT that either trial is free of bias -- NO RISK-OF-BIAS ASSESSMENT IS RECORDED. NOT anything about the excluded open-label trial, which reports a large effect on its own terms and is excluded on COMPARATOR TYPE, not on quality. NOT RSV hospitalisation or mortality, neither of which is the pooled endpoint. NOT reliability at k=2 -- see Hartung-Knapp.

handbook_authority.handbook: Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions
handbook_authority.c62: 'Undertake (or display) a meta-analysis only if participants, interventions, comparisons and outcomes are judged to be sufficiently similar to ensure an answer that is clinically meaningful.'

house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.estimator: REML with Hartung-Knapp, t on k-1 = 1 degree(s) of freedom (t = 12.7062)
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.THE_POINT_ESTIMATE_IS_UNCHANGED: The published point is 0.2605 and the house-rule point is 0.2606. THE NUMBER A READER REMEMBERS DOES NOT MOVE; what differs is the precision claim. That is why nothing downstream catches this -- every memorable quantity survives.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.variance_inflation_floor: A FLOOR OF 1 IS APPLIED TO THE VARIANCE-INFLATION FACTOR so the adjustment can never NARROW an interval below the unadjusted one. That guard is the recognised modification for exactly this instability, and its existence is evidence the small-k behaviour is a KNOWN problem with KNOWN handling rather than a novel judgement.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.no_rule_is_decided_here: The house rule is REML with Hartung-Knapp below k=10, settled days ago. Whether it means ALWAYS or WITH A FLOOR AT k=3 is a decision about this corpus, not a computation, and it has been referred rather than taken. BOTH INTERVALS STAND ON THIS PAGE UNTIL IT IS MADE. Nothing is unpublished and no reader is left with only the narrower one.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.what_this_means_for_this_pool: THE PUBLISHED INTERVAL EXCLUDES 1 AND THE HOUSE-RULE INTERVAL CROSSES IT. A SIGNIFICANCE VERDICT TURNS ON THE INTERVAL METHOD ALONE. A reader shown only the published interval has been told something firmer than the evidence supports; a reader shown only the wider one loses that the contributing trials agree. BOTH ARE HERE.
house_rule_interval_2026_08_18.read_the_width_with_care: AT k=2 HARTUNG-KNAPP USES t ON ONE DEGREE OF FREEDOM -- 12.7062 against the normal 1.9600 -- and the interval is enormously wider. That width is a property of the method at very few studies, not a measurement of this evidence. It is recorded so a reader can see it; it is NOT presented as the better interval.

r_output._what_this_is: Console output of the fit as printed. NOT re-typed and NOT summarised.
r_output.call: rma(yi = yi, sei = sei, method = "REML") and the same fit with test="knha"
r_output.inputs_derivation: yi = log(point); sei = (log(ci_high) - log(ci_low)) / (2 * 1.959964), read from this object's own per_trial rows.
r_output.what_k_equals_2_means: Two trials cannot inform a between-study variance; tau^2 is estimated with ONE degree of freedom. tau^2 is exactly 0 here and Q is 0.0879 on 1 df (p = 0.7668) -- the two trials agree closely -- but AT k = 2 THAT IS CONSISTENT WITH AGREEMENT, NOT EVIDENCE OF IT.

POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.a_a_published_review_pools_six_trials_wh: A PUBLISHED SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF THIS AGENT INCLUDED SIX RANDOMISED TRIALS (n = 12,086) WHERE THIS POOL CARRIES TWO. Lien et al., Pediatrics and Neonatology 2026, PMID 41314935, reports RSV-related hospitalisation at OR 0.19 (0.13 to 0.30) and severe RSV infection at OR 0.23 (0.12 to 0.44). Those are different outcomes on a different scale from this pool's medically attended RSV LRTI risk ratio of 0.2605 (0.1766 to 0.3845), so NO DISCREPANCY IS CLAIMED -- the point is the trial count.
POOL_FINDINGS_2026_08_21.b_which_four_are_missing_is_not_establis: The review's abstract names none of its six trials and no included-study table was read, so the four trials this object does not carry are COUNTED AND NOT IDENTIFIED. Naming them would require reading the review.

display_change_announced.what_changed: `heterogeneity.i2` and `heterogeneity.tau2` are field names that each map to more than one standard definition. Every number is unchanged; each now carries the definition it holds. tau2's definition was already recoverable from the declared `estimator` beside it and is copied, never inferred. i2's was not recoverable and is DECIDED BY RECOMPUTING BOTH FORMS from this object's own per-trial inputs, with the evidence recorded.
display_change_announced.why: A reader recomputing Higgins I-squared from the Q printed beside it would have concluded the object was wrong -- and would have been behaving exactly as we want readers to behave. An ambiguous label on an unambiguous number is a defect specifically against the only reader we claim to serve.

display_change_announced.what_changed: RoB 2 per result from the registrations (both SOME_CONCERNS, D2/D3 NO_INFORMATION); GRADE MODERATE; published comparison with a denominator (39/39/39/1/0); model output refit in R 4.6.0 / metafor 5.0.1, reproducing the stored point.

ceiling.statement: A domain that cannot be judged from the sources READ is NO_INFORMATION, never LOW. Low-by-default asserts a fact; high-by-default invents a defect. Overall is capped at SOME_CONCERNS wherever a domain is NO_INFORMATION.
ceiling.shape_note: A DICT, NOT A STRING -- registry class 70.

risk_of_bias.ONE_ASSESSOR_ONLY: ASSESSED BY ONE ASSESSOR. Under the standing specification that RoB 2 must be complete and done by TWO AIs from different model families, THIS IS INCOMPLETE. `rob2.assessors` is deliberately NOT written: a field whose presence would assert a two-assessor procedure that did not happen must stay absent.

grade.approach: GRADE, following the Cochrane Handbook chapter 14. Randomised evidence starts HIGH and is rated down with reasons.
grade.not_rated_up: No domain is rated UP. Rating up applies to observational evidence; these are randomised trials starting HIGH.

steps.reason: Both results are SOME_CONCERNS, and the driver is NOT an observed weakness -- D1, D4 and D5 are LOW on read registrations, with quadruple masking including the outcomes assessor. D2 and D3 are NO_INFORMATION because the registry does not carry those fields, and an unjudgeable domain caps the overall.

The stored refit gives tau^2 EXACTLY ZERO, Q 0.0879 on 1 df, p = 0.7668; the two intervals -- 0.2715 (0.1689 to 0.4363) and 0.2395 (0.1214 to 0.4727) -- overlap almost entirely and agree in conclusion.

One registered primary on each trial, the same endpoint, placebo-controlled, and it is exactly what is pooled. RECORDED AND NOT USED TO DOWNGRADE: the two trials enrol different infant populations and NCT02878330 fixes a 50 mg dose where MELODY uses weight-banded dosing -- read from the registered arm labels. The endpoint definition is unaffected.

The effect is large and the interval excludes no difference by a wide margin: 0.2605 (0.1766 to 0.3845). Even the Hartung-Knapp interval at k = 2, 0.2606 (0.1233 to 0.5505) on t = 12.7062 with 1 df, EXCLUDES 1 across its whole range. Downgrading for imprecision here would be mechanical rather than warranted.
k = 2. Funnel-plot asymmetry tests have essentially no power below about ten trials (Handbook 13.3.5.4), so this is NOT ASSESSABLE rather than 'undetected'.

primary.summary: MODERATE certainty. The single downgrade is for two unjudgeable risk-of-bias domains that the registry does not carry -- not for inconsistency, indirectness or imprecision, none of which the evidence supports downgrading.

reviews.title: Efficacy of nirsevimab for the prevention of RSV disease in infants: A systematic review, meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials, and global perspectives on recommendations and unmet needs
reviews.trial_set_basis: NOT READ. No included-study list in the abstract.
reviews.estimate_quoted: hospitalisation OR 0.19 (0.13 to 0.30); severe RSV infection OR 0.23 (0.12 to 0.44)
reviews.why_not_comparable: DIFFERENT OUTCOMES AND SCALE. They pool hospitalisation and severe infection as odds ratios; this object pools MEDICALLY ATTENDED RSV LRTI as a risk ratio. The estimates are of the same broad direction and magnitude but are not estimates of one quantity, so no discrepancy is claimed.

published_comparison.THE_FINDING_OF_THIS_COMPARISON_2026_08_2: A COVERAGE FINDING, NOT AN ESTIMAND ONE. Lien et al. 2026 included SIX randomised trials totalling 12,086 participants; THIS OBJECT POOLS TWO, totalling 4,465 as registered. Which six is NOT ESTABLISHED -- the abstract names none and no included-study table was read -- so the four this object does not carry are counted and not identified. THIS IS NOT A CLASS-76 INSTANCE: they did not choose a better-defined target, they pooled more of the same kind. Whether this review's search should be widened is a content decision.
